analysis.title: Five Asian Charts to Watch... 22 Nov 2026
key_insights: Author frames the market as in transition. Uncertainty drives capital toward perceived safety and demands a larger discount to fair value, producing multiple de-rating. Globally capital can move from Asia to the US, and within Asia/EM mandates between markets.
Many Asian markets are in correction or bear-market territory but the global economy is not in recession. Advice is neither to hide nor chase, favor selectivity, and be cautious on crowded trades.

GS US Equity Volatility Panic Index reads 9.7 out of 10, signalling genuine market stress. 15 prior prints above 9.5 preceded S&P 500 gains averaging 4.6% over 3 months (80% hit rate) and 9% over 6 months (73% hit rate), but the sample is small and April 2025 readings above 9 persisted for weeks.

Netease (9988 HK) is cited as a crowding example. Mutual funds are about 25bp overweight, short interest is low, and Southbound owns only 2% of float, so there are few natural bids to cushion a sell-off after a miss.
Asian hedge funds struggled MTD November but drawdowns were contained versus steep October declines. Global Prime book saw large net selling driven by long sales, led by North America and Asia.
Asian Info Tech/AI saw heavy net selling with long sales exceeding short sales 2.4 to 1. EM led the de-grossing over DM.
Net allocation to Asia in the Global Prime book fell 260bp MTD to 24.3%, an 8.2% overweight versus MSCI World. This is down from a 20% overweight in mid-June and back to late-January levels.
India is called an outperformer. It has lagged the region two consecutive years, rare in 30 years, and trades well below trend versus MXAPJ. Nifty is up 24% MTD relative to MSCI EM.

Foreigners bought $3.5bn of Indian equities last week, $3.8bn the prior week and $5.2bn in the first week of November. MTD buying of $12.5bn is 70% of YTD inflows. Author expects EM and Asia mandates to rotate from North Asia/China into India.

Copper is described as another crowded trade. ASX Metals and Mining fell 13% and the GS Global Copper Exposed Index fell 17% on the week, driven by a strong dollar, CTA selling, AI unwind and Druckenmiller's short copper comment.

GS's Camille Cerisey says copper is washing out, not breaking down, with mechanical positioning rather than fundamentals driving the move. The Global Copper Basket (GSXGCOPP) is down close to 35% from August peaks versus LME -22% and MXWO -8%.
